text: Fertilizer / top-dress schedule (ការប្រើប្រាស់ជី, បំប់ន). Radish requires balanced nutrition, especially nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) — soil/fertilizer selection should ensure these are available. Basal organic manure (well-rotted, chicken manure preferred, pig manure also usable) is applied before planting at roughly 8,000-10,000 kg per hectare. Beyond the basal application, top-dress fertilizer is applied in up to 4 stages according to crop need: (1) an early top-dress roughly 10 days after sowing, using a dissolved water-soluble fertilizer applied by watering can; (2) a second top-dress around 15-18 days after sowing, using compound NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer at roughly 200g per 10m² (~200 kg/ha), applied between rows after loosening the soil; (3) a third application around 25-30 days after sowing, using urea dissolved in water and applied by watering; (4) an optional fourth application around 40 days after sowing, combining urea and a potassium-type fertilizer, to help roots grow larger with better quality.
caveat: The specific per-application gram/kg figures for steps 1, 3, and 4 were read from dense small-font body text and are only moderately confident; recommend spot-checking against a clean high-resolution scan before using these as exact farmer-facing dosage figures. Step 2's ~200g/10m² figure was more clearly legible.
